_README: Floors for ci/check_suite_productivity.py — the counts below which a pytest step is
not doing its job, whatever its exit code says.
WHY A COMMITTED FILE AND NOT A FLAG.  A floor that can be lowered by a command-line
argument is a waiver with a flag: the lane that most needs the floor is the lane whose
author is under pressure to get past it.  Lowering a floor here is an edit to a tracked
file, in a diff, next to a `provenance` string that has to be rewritten to stay true.
WHY `min_collected` IS THE STRONG ONE.  The collected count does not depend on a GPU, an
ICD, a driver, an ORT build or an environment variable — it is the same number on every
lane and every developer machine.  So it can be a real ratchet.  `min_executed` cannot:
skip counts legitimately differ between lanes, so its floor is set from the WEAKEST
environment that still counts as running (no EP library, no Vulkan ICD, optional deps
absent).  Nothing that is working can execute less than that.
HOW TO RE-MEASURE.  Run the suite, then read the number this check itself reports:
python -m pytest tests/ops -q --tb=short -p no:randomly 2>&1 | tee run.log
python ci/check_suite_productivity.py --suite tests/ops run.log
`min_target_blocks` (libtest only).  A `cargo test --test a --test b` step is several
claims under one exit code, and a SUM cannot see one of them going silent: four small
targets summing to 11 and three of them summing to 11 with the fourth printing
`running 0 tests` are the same number.  `min_target_blocks` floors the count of
`test result:` blocks, and the checker separately fails — by target name — if any
single block executed zero.  Set it wherever a step names more than one `--test`.

provenance: 2026-08-03, Link. min_collected: 665 items collected, measured identically in two
independent Python environments on the same tree — the developer environment
(anaconda 3.12, all of tests/requirements.txt installed) and a scratch venv built
WITHOUT the optional `onnx-shape-inference` package. The two agreeing is the point:
the collected count is meant to be environment-independent, and before 2026-08-03
it was not — a module-level import of that optional package in
tests/ops/test_shape_inference_delta.py aborted collection of the whole directory,
taking all 665 to 0. Floor set 5 below the measured value: enough headroom that a
single test being renamed or merged does not redden the lane, small enough that a
file failing to import cannot hide.
min_executed '*' = 300: measured 316 executed (311 passed + 5 failed) in the scratch
venv with NO EP library, NO Vulkan ICD and the optional dependency absent — i.e. the
least capable environment in which this suite can still be said to have run. A lane
with a GPU and an EP must execute at least as many. If a real lane ever legitimately
executes fewer than 300, that is a finding about the lane, not about this number.
The per-lane keys are set equal to '*' deliberately, and are NOT calibrated from a
real CI run — nobody has measured build-test-linux or build-test-windows executed
counts from inside those runners yet. Stating that here rather than inventing two
tighter numbers: an uncalibrated floor that says so is honest; a fabricated one
reads exactly like a measured one.
2026-08-03, Link. A single-test selector, and therefore the exact shape the sweep
was looking for: a node id that stops matching — renamed test, renamed file, moved
class — makes pytest run nothing. This lane step has no other content, so 'ran zero
tests' and 'the no-ICD fallback works' would be indistinguishable in the log.
Floor of 1 is not a guess; it is the whole suite.
2026-08-03, Link, measured on Windows at main 607056a merged into squad/link:
`test result: ok. 510 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`.
Rust's libtest has exactly the same hole as pytest, and a quieter one: a target
with no tests prints `running 0 tests` / `test result: ok.` and exits ZERO. There
is no --strict flag for it. Eleven of the two device lanes' steps are `cargo test`
invocations, so the defect class does not stop at Python.
`ignored` maps to skipped and `filtered out` to deselected: neither executed. The
floor is 500 against 510 executed — the same ~1% headroom as tests/ops, for the
same reason. Only the --lib step is wired today; the five integration-target steps
are a NAMED, OPEN gap recorded in the sweep, not an oversight.
2026-08-03, Link, measured on Windows at main d46327b merged into squad/link:
`test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`
(bench/results/link-suite-productivity/cargo-test-layering-windows.log).
This is Tank's architectural lint: ops code must never import sys::, the ORT C
ABI, ash::, vk::, or use unsafe. Every one of its 26 tests is a SOURCE screen —
it needs no device, no ICD and no ORT, so the same number is expected on every
lane and the executed floor is set equal to the collected floor. If Linux and
Windows ever disagree here, that disagreement is itself the finding. Confirmed
on Linux (WSL Ubuntu) 2026-08-03: 26, the same number.
Floor 24 against 26: two tests of headroom. A lint whose tests were all
#[cfg]-ed out prints `running 0 tests` and exits 0, and the step's own exit code
cannot tell that from a clean tree — which is the entire content of a lint step.
2026-08-03, Link, measured on Windows at main d46327b merged into squad/link:
`test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`
(bench/results/link-suite-productivity/cargo-test-portability-windows.log).
Rules P1/P3. This lint is the reason the OrtLoggingLevel width defect is caught
on the lane that is NOT affected by it: MSVC types the enum c_int and GCC c_uint,
so a spelled i32 compiles on Windows and fails on Linux hours later, behind
everything else. A portability lint that silently ran zero tests would restore
exactly the state that cost a day on 2026-08-02.
8 -> 14 tests on 2026-08-02 when P3 was added. The floor is 12, so the four
P3 tests cannot be removed without an edit here.
Confirmed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu) 2026-08-03: 14, the same number
(bench/results/link-suite-productivity/cargo-test-portability-linux.log).
2026-08-03, Link, measured on Windows at main d46327b merged into squad/link
(bench/results/link-suite-productivity/cargo-test-integration-windows.log):
cdylib_load          1 passed
dump_capabilities    6 passed
host_registration    1 passed
validation_control   3 passed
-- 11 executed across 4 target blocks.
min_target_blocks = 4 IS THE LOAD-BEARING NUMBER HERE, not min_collected. This
step is four claims under one exit code, and three of the four targets are small
enough that an aggregate floor cannot see one of them go silent: cdylib_load and
host_registration are ONE test each. A floor of 10 against 11 executed leaves
exactly one test of headroom, and if that headroom were widened at all,
cdylib_load — the only thing in either lane that proves the shipped cdylib can be
dlopen'd — could vanish under it without changing the step's colour.
So the per-target rule does the work instead: check_suite_productivity.py fails
with condition=target_ran_nothing if ANY block executed zero, naming the target,
and with condition=targets_below_floor if a --test argument is dropped from the
step or a [[test]] target is removed from Cargo.toml. Those two are the shapes a
silent deletion actually takes; the sum is not.
These four targets load the cdylib and query Vulkan capabilities, so the counts
are in principle host-dependent -- but every one of them is written to report a
capability rather than require it. Confirmed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu, llvmpipe) by
ci/link-linux-repro/link_linux_target_counts.sh: the same 1/6/1/3 = 11 across 4
target blocks (bench/results/link-suite-productivity/cargo-test-integration-
linux.log). An earlier draft of this string credited link_linux_downstream.sh
for that number before any Linux run had produced it; it had not, and a
provenance string asserting a measurement nobody took is the same defect this
whole file exists to prevent. The script above is the one that took it.
2026-08-03, Link. NOT MEASURED, and saying so is the point: this floor is 1
because no measurement is needed to know that zero is not a census. The
conformance lane is workflow_dispatch-only and its pytest step is deliberately
`continue-on-error: true` plus `|| true` — it is declared non-evidence under
DESIGN.md 10.0 because it carries no attribution.
The zero-work sweep ACCEPTED that step on those grounds and the acceptance was
half right. It holds for the step; it does not hold for the artifact. The step's
`conformance.out` is an input to ci/check_fatal_log.py two steps later, so an
all-skipped or never-collected census produced a green fatal-log step reporting
that it had scanned a log — a blind witness counted as a witness.
So this floor enforces exactly the distinction the acceptance always rested on
and never checked: conformance cases that FAIL are tolerated, a census that DID
NOT RUN is not. A real floor here would need a measured onnx-tests run on the
runner, which nobody has done; inventing a tighter number would read exactly
like a measured one.
2026-08-03, Link, measured on this tree after this round's 8 new tests landed:
125 collected, 122 passed + 3 failed (the three known census reds). The host-free
lane's own suite had the same hole it
exists to close in others: if ci/ stopped importing, this step would have reported
success for collecting nothing — and it is the step that certifies every other
check in ci/. Executed counts failures deliberately: a failing test is evidence
that its subject was exercised.
